This work presents FE-MAD (Finite Element-Based Material learning via Automatic Differentiation), an end-to-end differentiable framework that integrates a constitutive neural network model within a JAX-FEM nonlinear solver and identifies its parameters through gradient-based minimization of a measurement-mismatch loss. Newton tangent stiffness and loss gradients are computed automatically using forward- and reverse-mode automatic differentiation throughout the entire pipeline, thereby removing the need for analytic adjoints or offline surrogate models. FE-MAD is demonstrated for two architectures: a grey-box Constitutive Artificial Neural Network (CANN), a polyconvex, fully connected model with high flexibility, and a white-box CANN, an expert-system network with phenomenologically interpretable strain-energy terms. Focusing on incompressible isotropic hyperelasticity, FE-MAD is evaluated on three open experimental datasets: (1) full digital image correlation (DIC) of a perforated tensile specimen, (2) a reduced-data scenario with a one-dimensional stretch profile and global force-displacement curve, and (3) a heterogeneous matrix-inclusion system in which both phases constitutive laws are identified and generalized to twenty-two previously unseen samples.
tldr: This paper presents a finite element-based framework for learning constitutive neural network models from full-field deformation data using automatic differentiation.
motivation: Traditional calibration methods for material models rely on homogeneous stress-strain experiments, which are often impractical; heterogeneous full-field data offers a more robust alternative but existing approaches face trade-offs between generality, robustness, and computational efficiency.
method: FE-MAD integrates a constitutive neural network within a JAX-FEM nonlinear solver and uses automatic differentiation (forward and reverse mode) to compute gradients for parameter identification via gradient-based minimization of a measurement-mismatch loss.
result: The framework is demonstrated on three experimental datasets for incompressible isotropic hyperelasticity, showing successful identification of constitutive parameters for both grey-box and white-box CANN architectures, including generalization to unseen samples.
conclusion: FE-MAD provides an end-to-end differentiable approach that eliminates the need for analytic adjoints or surrogate models, offering a computationally efficient and robust method for material learning from full-field data.

title: A Differentiable Machine Learning Small-angle X-ray Scattering Analysis Framework For Structure Elucidation Of Lipid Nanoparticles
authors: Maria B{\aa}nkestad, Sandra Barman, Magnus R\"oding, Erik Kaunisto, Viktoriia Meklesh, Audrey Gallud, Marco Mendez, Marianna Yanez Arteta, Stefan Norberg, Ann Terry, Smita Chakraborty, Shun Yu, Jerk R\"onnols, Sepideh Pashami
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are efficient delivery systems for negatively charged nucleic acids. Their multi-component architecture yields a core-shell structure. Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) is an important characterization technique for LNPs, but recovering internal structure and size distribution from SAXS is an inverse problem with non-unique solutions. Realistic models are often too expensive for systematic exploration. We introduce a machine-learning-accelerated, differentiable framework for SAXS analysis of heterogeneous, polydisperse LNPs. The forward model combines a core-shell particle with a Gaussian random-field interior, a neural surrogate for the monodisperse SAXS map, and a differentiable layer integrating over particle-size distributions. The surrogate reduces prediction cost by four orders of magnitude, while differentiability enables large-scale multi-start fitting and ensemble identifiability analysis. Applied to synthetic and experimental MC3 LNP data, the framework shows that near-identical SAXS fits can arise from distinct parameter modes, with the experimental fits dominated by a trade-off between size-distribution and interior-structure parameters.
tldr: A machine-learning-accelerated SAXS analysis framework for lipid nanoparticles is introduced, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To address the inverse problem of recovering internal structure and size distribution from SAXS data for lipid nanoparticles, which is computationally expensive with realistic models.
method: The framework combines a core-shell particle model with a Gaussian random-field interior, a neural surrogate for the monodisperse SAXS map, and a differentiable layer for integrating over particle-size distributions.
result: The surrogate reduces prediction cost by four orders of magnitude, and the framework reveals that near-identical SAXS fits can arise from distinct parameter modes, with trade-offs between size-distribution and interior-structure parameters.
conclusion: The framework enables efficient multi-start fitting and identifiability analysis, but its application is specific to lipid nanoparticle characterization and not relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Multi-Fidelity Learning With Shallow Recurrent Decoders For Reactor Physics
authors: Stefano Riva, Carolina Introini, J. Nathan Kutz, Antonio Cammi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In reactor physics, neutronics can be treated with different fidelity levels, according to the needs of the user. On one hand, the precise modeling of neutrons' behaviour in reactor physics is often expensive and time-consuming due to the high computational costs to numerically solve the Boltzmann transport equation. Conversely, by adopting suitable assumptions, such as the SP[MATH], diffusion theory, and point kinetics, it is possible to generate efficiently low-fidelity data. From the perspective of surrogate models, this computational limitation translates into a scarcity of high-fidelity data and a significant amount of low-fidelity data. Given this difference in fidelity levels, it would be interesting to develop a suitable procedure to map low-fidelity models towards higher fidelity models; for instance, one could obtain the solution to a multi-group diffusion equation starting from time-series data obtained from a point kinetics model. Indeed, this work investigates this possibility by leveraging multi-fidelity information with Shallow Recurrent Decoders, a novel machine learning architecture able to map time-series observations to the full state of the reactor. This technique has been designed to use local or global measurements as input and map their temporal trajectories to the high-dimensional state; by the same logic, in principle, this architecture can also be used when the input is formed by the solution of a lumped model. This work applies this idea to a benchmark reactor geometry, mapping the point kinetics model to the diffusion solution under various input conditions, with much less computational costs.
tldr: This paper uses multi-fidelity learning with shallow recurrent decoders to map low-fidelity point kinetics models to high-fidelity diffusion solutions in reactor physics.
motivation: High-fidelity neutronics simulations are computationally expensive, while low-fidelity models are cheap but inaccurate. The authors aim to develop a surrogate model that leverages abundant low-fidelity data to predict high-fidelity states efficiently.
method: They employ Shallow Recurrent Decoders, a machine learning architecture that maps time-series observations (from low-fidelity models) to the full high-dimensional state of the reactor, using a multi-fidelity learning framework.
result: The method successfully maps point kinetics model outputs to diffusion solutions for a benchmark reactor geometry under various input conditions, achieving much lower computational costs than direct high-fidelity simulations.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates potential for efficient surrogate modeling in reactor physics, but its applicability to other domains or more complex physics remains to be explored.

title: Time-frequency Analysis Of Nonlinear Compton Scattering Via Joint Probability Distributions
authors: Daniel Seipt Nikita Larin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interaction of charged particles with an intense laser pulse gives rise to a number of characteristic spectral features of emitted radiation, including the generation of harmonics, spectral broadening due to the phase-dependent ponderomotive red shift, and the emergence of intricate sub-harmonic structures. These effects are accumulated over the course of the interaction with the electromagnetic field and are therefore inherently nonlocal in nature. For a deeper understanding of strong-field quantum electrodynamics (SFQED) processes and their practical applications, it is desirable to employ tools that enable simultaneous analysis in the time and energy domains. In time-frequency analysis, such tools are provided by joint distributions (JDs). In this work, we demonstrate how a JD can be devised within the SFQED framework. Specifically, we focus on constructing a non-negative JD, which allows for a clear probabilistic interpretation. We study the properties of the proposed distribution and test its utility by applying it to the nonlinear Compton scattering in complex laser pulse configurations with carrier-envelope phase and variable polarization.
tldr: This paper introduces a non-negative joint probability distribution for time-frequency analysis of nonlinear Compton scattering in strong-field QED.
motivation: To understand spectral features like harmonics and ponderomotive red shift that are nonlocal in time, requiring simultaneous time-energy analysis.
method: Constructs a non-negative joint distribution within the SFQED framework and applies it to nonlinear Compton scattering with complex laser pulses.
result: Demonstrates the utility of the joint distribution for analyzing carrier-envelope phase and polarization effects.
conclusion: Provides a new tool for time-frequency analysis in SFQED, with potential applications to other strong-field processes.

title: Spatial Resolution Of X-ray Beam-tracking Microscopy
authors: Harry Allan, Carlos Navarrete-Le\'on, Adam Doherty, Shashidhara Marathe, Kaz Wanelik, Marco Endrizzi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: X-ray beam-tracking is a phase-contrast imaging technique capable of simultaneously retrieving transmission, phase, and dark-field images. Although the spatial resolution in beam-tracking is largely considered to be 'aperture driven', no model yet exists to describe this in full. The dark-field channel is of particular interest, due to previous observations of anomalously high sharpness compared to transmission and phase channels. We derive a full optical transfer function model for each contrast channel using the Fokker-Planck equation for near-field imaging. Experimental validation using both synchrotron-based and laboratory-based setups, with 15 um circular and 10 um rectangular apertures, reveals a limiting resolution of at least 3 um, much smaller than the apertures themselves. Together, the model and the supporting experiments offer a full description of spatial resolution in beam-tracking, and formally confirm the greater spatial resolution in the dark-field channel. These findings open new possibilities in system design and experimental protocols to exploit these capabilities.
tldr: This paper develops an optical transfer function model for X-ray beam-tracking microscopy, demonstrating that spatial resolution in the dark-field channel can exceed aperture size.
motivation: To understand and quantify the spatial resolution limits in X-ray beam-tracking phase-contrast imaging, especially the anomalously high sharpness observed in the dark-field channel.
method: Derived a full optical transfer function model using the Fokker-Planck equation for near-field imaging, validated with synchrotron and laboratory experiments using circular and rectangular apertures.
result: The model and experiments show a limiting resolution of at least 3 µm, much smaller than the 10-15 µm apertures, and confirm higher resolution in the dark-field channel.
conclusion: The findings enable improved system design and experimental protocols to exploit the high-resolution dark-field channel in X-ray imaging.

title: Opinion Dynamics On Social Proximity Disordered Networks
authors: Fellipe Aranha, Giuliano G. Porci\'uncula, Adauto J. F. de Souza, Paulo R. A. Campos, Andr\'e L. M. Vilela
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how local social pressure shapes collective opinion formation is essential in modern society, with implications in sociology, politics, finance, and technology. Complex networks are a powerful framework for investigating these processes and for representing social interactions in emergent phenomena, and canonical models such as random, scale-free, and small-world networks remain most relevant when Euclidean geometric proximity and contiguous interactions are not the dominant organizing factors. Our investigation explores the effects of Gabriel graphs, a spatially embedded network that utilizes proximity-based interactions, on social opinion dynamics. Using a geometric disorder parameter that randomly displaces agent coordinates, we transition from square lattices of social interactions to spatial random networks that preserve local constraints while introducing strong topological heterogeneity. Opinion dynamics operate through social pressure, with a level of nonconformity that affects dissent among opinions. We analyze magnetization, susceptibility, and Binder's fourth-order cumulant to characterize the emergence and breakdown of global social consensus. The model exhibits second-order phase transitions whose behavior depends on both geometric disorder and nonconformity levels. We use volumetric scaling and provide a reference frame appropriate for characterizing criticality in regular and heterogeneous interaction topologies. We find that the standard critical exponents remain compatible with the two-dimensional Ising universality class. Furthermore, the results suggest that spatially constrained, planar, and globally connected interaction topologies preserve the dimensionality of space in critical dynamics analysis.
tldr: This paper studies opinion dynamics on spatially embedded networks with geometric disorder, finding that the critical behavior remains in the 2D Ising universality class.
motivation: To understand how local social pressure and network topology affect collective opinion formation, particularly in spatially constrained systems.
method: They use Gabriel graphs with a geometric disorder parameter to interpolate between square lattices and spatial random networks, and simulate opinion dynamics with a nonconformity parameter, analyzing magnetization, susceptibility, and Binder cumulant.
result: The model exhibits second-order phase transitions; critical exponents are compatible with the 2D Ising universality class, indicating that spatial constraints preserve the dimensionality in critical dynamics.
conclusion: Spatially embedded planar networks maintain the 2D Ising critical behavior, suggesting that the dimensionality of space is a key factor in opinion dynamics on such networks.

title: A Stochastic Model For Fog Forecasting
authors: Boualem Khouider Elsa Cardoso-Bihlo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite significant advancements in parameterizations of boundary layer processes, forecasting, and nowcasting low-level clouds using numerical models remain challenging. The purpose of this study is to test a prototype of a high-resolution stochastic-deterministic model designed to simulate the life cycle of fog cover based on the Ising model from statistical mechanics. The case of advection fog around St. John's Airport in Newfoundland (Canada) has been considered. The model demonstrates promising capabilities in forecasting mean fog cover and replicating the horizontal structure observed in satellite imagery, including bands, rolls, and closed or open cells. We evaluate the model's predictive skill by analyzing its effectiveness in reproducing the evolution of fog cover across three representative cases. A contingency table and associated performance metrics are used to assess its accuracy.
tldr: This paper uses an Ising model from statistical mechanics to simulate advection fog cover, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Fog forecasting is challenging for numerical models; the authors aim to test a stochastic-deterministic model based on the Ising model to improve predictions.
method: A high-resolution stochastic-deterministic model based on the Ising model is developed and applied to advection fog cases around St. John's Airport, Newfoundland.
result: The model shows promising capabilities in forecasting mean fog cover and replicating horizontal structures like bands and cells observed in satellite imagery.
conclusion: The model may be useful for fog nowcasting, but further validation and development are needed.

title: Stereotyping By Strategy Standing Diversifies Cooperation Patterns In Indirect Reciprocity
authors: Ming Wei, Xin Wang, Wenqiang Zhu, Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Feng Fu, Shaoting Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indirect reciprocity explains how cooperation evolves through social reputations. People observe others, assign reputations, and condition their future actions on these assignments. This process is cognitively demanding, and stereotyping offers a simpler alternative by replacing individual-level reputation with group-level information. Theoretical models commonly implement stereotyping through exogenously given group labels. In real societies, however, group-level impressions may be associated with observable patterns of behavior. Here we propose a framework of stereotyping by strategy standing, in which mutants may condition their actions on the overall reputation level associated with a resident strategy rather than on the recipient's reputation. We show that this form of stereotyping can diversify stable cooperation in indirect reciprocity. As the strength of stereotyping increases, additional cooperative evolutionarily stable norm-strategy (ESS) pairs emerge in substantial numbers. In particular, we identify eight highly cooperative ESS pairs that become stable under very weak stereotyping. These pairs, which we call the counterparts of the leading eight, share the same social norms as the classical leading eight and differ only in how they prescribe behavior between bad individuals. They are unstable without stereotyping because they can be invaded by their corresponding leading strategies, but they become stable once stereotyping exceeds a critical threshold. Our results suggest that group-level impressions based on strategy standing can provide a coarse-grained informational route to stable cooperation and offer a more behaviorally grounded perspective on how stereotyping affects indirect reciprocity.
tldr: This paper studies how stereotyping based on strategy standing can diversify cooperation patterns in indirect reciprocity, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand how group-level impressions (stereotyping) can stabilize cooperation in indirect reciprocity without requiring individual reputations.
method: Evolutionary game theory model where mutants condition actions on the overall reputation of a resident strategy rather than individual reputations; analysis of evolutionary stable strategies (ESS) under varying stereotyping strength.
result: Identified eight cooperative ESS pairs (counterparts of the leading eight) that become stable when stereotyping exceeds a critical threshold, diversifying cooperation patterns.
conclusion: Stereotyping based on strategy standing provides a behaviorally grounded route to stable cooperation, offering insights into the role of group-level information in social evolution.

title: Passively Synchronized Dual-color Mode-locked Fiber Lasers Based On Nonlinear Amplifying Loop Mirrors
authors: Jing Zeng, Bowen Li, Qiang Hao, Ming Yan, Kun Huang, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We have proposed and implemented a novel scheme for passive all-optical synchronization between erbium and ytterbium mode-locked fiber lasers. The passive locking of repetition rates for the dual-color pulses was realized by cross-phase modulation within phase-biased nonlinear amplifying loop mirrors. In contrast to previous demonstrations, the synchronization system was configured in an all-polarization-maintaining structure, thus gaining substantially improved stability and robustness. Consequently, the maximum tolerance of cavity-length mismatch of 16.2 mm was achieved unprecedentedly, which was at least one order of magnitude longer than previously reported results for comparable temporal durations of involved pulses. The corresponding relative timing jitter was measured to be 31 fs within 1-MHz bandwidth. Such tight and robust synchronization fiber laser system offers a great potential for various applications, such as pump-probe microscopy, Raman scattering spectroscopy and nonlinear frequency generation.
tldr: This paper presents a passively synchronized dual-color mode-locked fiber laser system using nonlinear amplifying loop mirrors, achieving robust synchronization with low jitter.
motivation: To improve the stability and robustness of passively synchronized dual-color fiber lasers for applications like pump-probe microscopy and nonlinear frequency generation.
method: The scheme uses cross-phase modulation within phase-biased nonlinear amplifying loop mirrors in an all-polarization-maintaining configuration.
result: Achieved a maximum cavity-length mismatch tolerance of 16.2 mm and a relative timing jitter of 31 fs within 1-MHz bandwidth.
conclusion: The demonstrated system offers tight and robust synchronization, promising for various applications, but is not directly related to the user's research interests.

title: Observation Of Spectral Mode Splitting In A Pump-enhanced Ring Cavity For Mid-infrared Generation
authors: Kun Huang, Jiwei Gan, Jing Zeng, Qiang Hao, Kangwen Yang, Ming Yan, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on experimental and theoretical investigation of mode-splitting dynamics in a ring cavity under the perturbation of fractional Bragg reflection from a periodically-poled nonlinear crystal. Counterintuitively, pronounced mode splitting in the spectral domain could been observed even with a tiny intensity reflection of 0.0003. The breaking of running-wave operation in the ring-cavity configuration resulted in comparable circulating fields in forward- and counter-propagation directions, which thus dramatically reduced the enhancing factor for the resonating field. In contrast, a linear cavity with intrinsically bidirectional operation was immune to the small intra-cavity reflection. Therefore, the linear-cavity layout could provide an expedient solution for a given internal reflection to obtain more stable and higher enhancement, which was confirmed by comparative studies of mid-infrared generation based on pump-enhanced difference frequency conversion. The underlying mechanism was further modeled by numerical simulations, which agreed well with experimental results. These findings could not only shed light on the understanding of the exotic feature of concatenated optical cavities, but also provide a useful guide to practical design of enhancement cavities for cavity-based frequency conversion with periodically-poled nonlinear crystals.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral mode splitting in a pump-enhanced ring cavity due to weak Bragg reflection from a nonlinear crystal, and compares it with linear cavities for mid-infrared generation.
motivation: To understand and mitigate the detrimental effect of intra-cavity reflections on the enhancement factor in ring cavities used for frequency conversion.
method: Experimental and theoretical study of mode splitting in a ring cavity with a periodically-poled nonlinear crystal, using numerical simulations and comparative experiments with linear cavities.
result: Even a tiny reflection (0.0003) causes significant mode splitting and reduces the enhancement factor in ring cavities, while linear cavities are immune to such small reflections.
conclusion: Linear cavities are more robust for pump-enhanced frequency conversion with periodically-poled crystals, providing a practical design guideline.

title: Controlled Generation Of Ultrafast Vector Vortex Beams From A Mode-locked Fiber Laser
authors: Kun Huang, Jing Zeng, Jiwei Gan, Qiang Hao, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on a new class of mode-locked fiber laser that allows direct creation of ultrafast vector vortex beams at arbitrary positions on the higher-order Poincar\'{e} sphere. The on-demand generation of space-variant polarization patterns was realized by controlling geometric phases inside the laser resonator to map polarization to orbital angular momentum. Thanks to the ingenious cavity design, the required intracavity manipulation of the geometric phase imposed no disturbance on the passively mode-locked operation, thus demonstrating robust and flexible switching of vectorial modes with a 8.5-ps pulse duration. Analytical expressions were deduced to model the generated cylindrically-symmetric polarization profiles, and agreed exceedingly well with experimental observations. The presented fiber laser would constitute a compact light source for producing ultrafast pulses in high-purity structured modes, which may find broad applications in classical and quantum optics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a mode-locked fiber laser that generates ultrafast vector vortex beams with controlled polarization patterns via geometric phase manipulation.
motivation: To create a compact, robust source of ultrafast structured light beams with arbitrary space-variant polarization for applications in classical and quantum optics.
method: A mode-locked fiber laser cavity is designed to control geometric phases, mapping polarization to orbital angular momentum without disturbing mode-locking, enabling on-demand generation of vector vortex beams.
result: The laser produces 8.5-ps pulses with cylindrically-symmetric polarization profiles that match analytical predictions, allowing flexible switching of vectorial modes.
conclusion: This fiber laser provides a practical source for high-purity structured ultrafast pulses, potentially useful in optical communication, quantum information, and other fields.

title: Aberration-Free Optical Spectrometer
authors: Qingze Guan, Zi Heng Lim, Xinchen Wan, Yixiu Shen, Guangya Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical spectrometers are fundamental to scientific analysis, yet achieving high performance at low cost remains challenging because uncorrected aberrations rapidly degrade spectral resolution and typically necessitate complex, expensive optics. Moreover, to preserve spectral resolution, many compact designs remain fundamentally throughput-limited in terms of having a high f-number and a narrow slit. Here we present SHADES (Stochastic High-throughput Aberration-free Deep-Encoded Spectrometer), a general framework that mitigates the effects of optical aberrations using a stochastic grating array (SGA) coupled with physically grounded deep learning (DL), while substantially increasing optical throughput using encoded multi-slits. We develop a theoretical framework establishing aberration resilient spectroscopy in compact, highly aberrated systems, enabling miniaturization without sacrificing spectral resolution and optical throughput. SHADES utilizes an arbitrary spectrum generator (ASG) for hardware-in-the-loop calibration with a DL-based reconstruction pipeline. We further leverage transfer learning (TL) to reduce calibration data and computation for scalable deployment of SHADES. Experimentally, a micro-SHADES prototype achieves a spectral resolution of 2.4 nm over 450-700 nm and accurately reconstructs fluorescence spectra for chemical identification. Collectively, SHADES provides an aberration-free, high-throughput, low-cost spectrometer architecture suited for compact and scalable sensing applications.
tldr: SHADES uses a stochastic grating array and deep learning to create a compact, high-throughput, aberration-free optical spectrometer.
motivation: To overcome the trade-off between spectral resolution, optical throughput, and cost in conventional spectrometers by mitigating aberrations without complex optics.
method: A stochastic grating array (SGA) is combined with physically grounded deep learning for reconstruction, and an arbitrary spectrum generator (ASG) enables hardware-in-the-loop calibration with transfer learning.
result: A micro-SHADES prototype achieves 2.4 nm resolution over 450-700 nm and accurately reconstructs fluorescence spectra.
conclusion: SHADES provides a low-cost, compact spectrometer architecture suitable for scalable sensing, with potential for further miniaturization and broader spectral ranges.

title: Optical Chirality Of Membrane Metasurfaces With Broken In-plane Symmetry
authors: Ivan Toftul, Brijesh Kumar, Maxim Gorkunov, Yuri Kivshar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study chiroptical properties of single-layer dielectric membrane metasurfaces with broken in-plane symmetry. In sharp contrast to a common belief that chiral optical phenomena require symmetry breaking in the vertical direction, we show that flat single-layer metasurfaces are capable of strong specific chiral effects. Although the single-layer geometry forbids conventional co-polarized circular dichroism, strong resonant conversion circular dichroism appears to be possible in particular wavelength ranges determined by the spectra of photonic eigenmodes. We explore its origin starting with a [MATH] rotation-symmetric and in-plane mirror-symmetric membrane metasurface and applying to it various in-plane perturbations. Simultaneously breaking of the in-plane mirror symmetry and lifting the rotation symmetry unlocks resonantly enhanced circular conversion dichroism. We derive selection rules for this effect and trace its origin to eigenmode interference and intercoupling using chiral coupled-mode theory.
tldr: This paper studies chiroptical effects in single-layer dielectric membrane metasurfaces with broken in-plane symmetry, showing that strong circular conversion dichroism can occur without vertical symmetry breaking.
motivation: To challenge the common belief that chiral optical phenomena require vertical symmetry breaking, and to explore the potential of flat single-layer metasurfaces for chiroptical applications.
method: The authors start with a rotation-symmetric and in-plane mirror-symmetric membrane metasurface, then apply in-plane perturbations. They use chiral coupled-mode theory to derive selection rules and trace the origin of circular conversion dichroism to eigenmode interference and intercoupling.
result: Strong resonant conversion circular dichroism is possible in single-layer metasurfaces when both in-plane mirror symmetry and rotation symmetry are broken, despite the absence of conventional co-polarized circular dichroism.
conclusion: The findings open new possibilities for chiroptical devices using simple planar geometries, with implications for sensing and polarization control.

title: On Leadership Emergence In Opinion Dynamics On Social Networks
authors: Martina Alutto, Lorenzo Zino, Karl H. Johansson, Angela Fontan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Leadership in social groups emerges dynamically through interaction and opinion exchange. Empirical evidence indicates that individuals expressing strong opinions tend to gain influence, while sustained leadership critically depends on maintaining alignment with the surrounding social context. Motivated by these observations, we introduce a coupled dynamical model describing the simultaneous evolution of opinions and leadership in a networked population. Extending the Friedkin-Johnsen framework, we represent leadership as a time-varying susceptibility to social influence, which evolves according to a game-theoretic mechanism, consistent with social psychology evidence. Within this setting, agents strengthen their leadership by expressing decisive yet socially coherent opinions, whereas misalignment with the collective state results in a loss of influence. We analyze the coupled dynamics and establish sufficient conditions to identify which agents necessarily emerge as leaders and which act as followers in the social network.
tldr: This paper models leadership emergence in social networks using a coupled opinion-leadership dynamics framework, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how leadership emerges dynamically through opinion exchange in social networks, motivated by empirical observations that strong opinions and social alignment influence leadership.
method: Extends the Friedkin-Johnsen opinion dynamics model by introducing a time-varying susceptibility to social influence that evolves via a game-theoretic mechanism, coupling opinion and leadership dynamics.
result: Establishes sufficient conditions to identify which agents necessarily become leaders and which become followers in the network.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical framework for leadership emergence in social networks, with potential applications in understanding social influence and group dynamics.

title: Design Of An Efficient Tunable Dual Narrow-band Mems Mid And Far Ir Emitter With Me-NTA For Industrial And Biomedical Applications
authors: Md. Imran Hasmi, Md. Saffat Gohor, Foez Ahmed, Jaker Hossain
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectrally selective infrared (IR) thermal emitters are gaining much attention now-a-days for sensing, spectroscopy and biomedical applications. In this research, two metasurface incorporated IR emitters are proposed and numerically analyzed using finite element method (FEM). First structure comprises a NiCr heater integrated with a NiCr-based metallic nanotube array (Me-NTA) metasurface to produce a single-narrowband emission in the mid-infrared (MIR) region. Furthermore, an Au-based Me-NTA metasurface on a NiCr-Au hybrid heater subsequently produces dual-narrowband emission in the short-and far-infrared (SIR and FIR) spectrums. Function of these emitters can be explained by Joule heating with the help of DC bias and consequently uniform temperature distribution can be observed along the active region. Simulation analysis shows that NiCr-metasurface based emitter produces single narrow-band near perfect emission centered at 4.5 {\mu}m in MIR region at an operating temperature of 700 K with maximum in-band conversion efficiency (CE) of 32.3% and radiated power of 199 mW. On the other hand, Au-metasurface based emitter generates dual-narrowband emission peaking at 2.5 {\mu}m and 10 {\mu}m, correlating to SIR and FIR subsequently, achieving maximum emission of 93% and 85%, respectively. The in-band CE for this emitter attains 10.4% and 4.4% in the first and second bands, associated with radiated powers of 350 mW and 147 mW, accordingly. Furthermore, execution of the emitter at 500 K reveals FIR emission with reduced power consumption. These results substantiate the possibilities of the suggested emitters in various industrial and biomedical applications.
tldr: This paper designs and simulates metasurface-based infrared thermal emitters for narrowband emission in MIR and FIR regions, targeting industrial and biomedical applications.
motivation: To develop spectrally selective IR emitters with high efficiency for sensing, spectroscopy, and biomedical uses.
method: Finite element method (FEM) simulations of two metasurface designs: NiCr-based metallic nanotube array (Me-NTA) for single-band MIR emission, and Au-based Me-NTA on NiCr-Au hybrid heater for dual-band SIR/FIR emission.
result: NiCr emitter achieves 32.3% conversion efficiency at 4.5 μm; Au emitter achieves 93% and 85% emission at 2.5 μm and 10 μm with 10.4% and 4.4% conversion efficiencies.
conclusion: The proposed emitters show potential for industrial and biomedical applications, but the paper focuses on device engineering rather than fundamental physics relevant to the user's interests.

title: Inverse Design Of Realizable Metasurface Based Absorbers Using Improved Conditioning And Diversity Enhanced Progressively Growing GANs
authors: Vineetha Joy, Mohammad Abdullah, Pramit Pal, Anshuman Kumar, Amit Sethi, Hema Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metasurfaces enable precise manipulation of electromagnetic waves for applications such as beam steering, sensing, and stealth technology. However, inverse design of metasurfaces with targeted EM responses remains challenging due to the computational expense of iterative full wave simulation driven optimization and the limited conditioning fidelity and diversity of existing generative approaches. To address these challenges, this paper presents a generative inverse design framework for controllable and physically consistent metasurface synthesis under continuous spectral constraints. The proposed approach employs a progressively growing Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty integrated with feature wise linear modulation based conditioning for stable propagation of continuous spectral and fabrication constraints. EM consistency is embedded directly into the generative learning process through a surrogate assisted spectral alignment loss, enabling physics constrained generation during training. Further, a determinantal point process based diversity regularization strategy is incorporated to generate geometrically diverse yet spectrally consistent realizations for the same target response. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through the generation of practically realizable metasurface absorbers exhibiting diverse reflection characteristics in the frequency range of 2 to 18 GHz. EM simulations validate that the generated designs meet the target specifications with high accuracy. The final proposed framework achieved an average mean squared error of 0.0052, diversity score of 0.8730, band alignment accuracy of 0.8533, and a valid EM design generation percentage of 89.57, clearly demonstrating its capability to generate highly accurate, diverse, electromagnetically consistent and fabrication realizable metasurface configurations.
tldr: This paper presents a generative inverse design framework for metasurface absorbers using improved GANs, focusing on electromagnetic wave manipulation.
motivation: Inverse design of metasurfaces is computationally expensive and existing generative methods lack fidelity and diversity.
method: A progressively growing Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty, feature-wise linear modulation conditioning, surrogate-assisted spectral alignment loss, and determinantal point process diversity regularization.
result: The framework achieves high accuracy (MSE 0.0052), diversity (0.8730), band alignment (0.8533), and 89.57% valid EM designs for metasurface absorbers in 2-18 GHz.
conclusion: The approach enables efficient generation of physically consistent and fabrication-realizable metasurface designs, with potential for broader EM applications.

title: Euler Scheme For Stochastic Functional Differential Equations Driven By Fractional Brownian Motion Via Fractional Calculus Techniques
authors: Alexander Abreu (CIMFAV), H\'ector Araya (UNAI), Lisandro Fermin (AMSE), Johanna Garz\'on (UNAL), Soledad Torres
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a stochastic functional differential equation (SFDE) with memory driven by a fractional Brownian motion (fBm) with Hurst parameter H>1/2. An Euler-type numerical scheme is proposed and analyzed under suitable regularity conditions on the drift and diffusion coefficients using tools from fractional calculus. We prove the convergence of the scheme and derive the corresponding rate in terms of the discretization step. Numerical simulations illustrate the theoretical results and confirm the accuracy of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper develops an Euler numerical scheme for stochastic functional differential equations driven by fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter >1/2, using fractional calculus techniques.
motivation: To provide a convergent numerical method for SFDEs with memory driven by fBm, which are important in modeling systems with long-range dependence.
method: An Euler-type scheme is proposed and analyzed using fractional calculus tools, with convergence rate derived under regularity conditions on drift and diffusion coefficients.
result: The scheme converges and the rate depends on the discretization step; numerical simulations confirm theoretical accuracy.
conclusion: The work contributes to numerical analysis of SFDEs with fBm, but has no direct connection to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pseudosymmetry, Ricci Soliton And Curvature Inheritance Symmetries Of Friedmann Lema\^itre Robertson Walker Spacetime
authors: Kamiruzzaman Absos Ali Shaikh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Friedmann--Lema\^{i}tre--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) spacetime, which was first proposed by Friedmann (1922--1924) and Lema\^{i}tre (1927) and subsequently developed by Robertson and Walker (1935), is an isotropic and homogeneous cosmological model of the universe. This paper addresses a significant gap in the differential geometry literature by providing a comprehensive examination of the curvature properties of the FLRW spacetime. It is demonstrated that the FLRW spacetime satisfies the curvature condition R \cdot R - Q(S, R)=L_C Q(g, C) alongside several pseudosymmetric-type conditions related to the conformal and conharmonic curvature tensors. Furthermore, the Tachibana tensors Q(g,C) and Q(S, C) are found to exhibit a linear dependence on the tensor [MATH]. Additionally, the spacetime is shown to be a 2-quasi-Einstein manifold, generalized Roter type and Ein(3). The Ricci tensor is shown to be neither cyclic parallel nor of Codazzi type, yet it satisfies several compatibility requirements concerning the R, C, P, K and W curvature tensors. A thorough analysis of Ricci solitons and curvature inheritance properties reveals that the spacetime admits almost Ricci soliton and [MATH]-Ricci Yamabe soliton structures with respect to the non-Killing soliton vector fields [MATH] and [MATH]. Moreover, the spacetime admits generalized curvature inheritance symmetry properties for the Riemann curvature tensor, as well as for the Weyl conformal, concircular, and conharmonic curvature tensors with respect to the coordinate vector field [MATH] and the gradient of [MATH]. Later, a comparison of the FLRW and Lema\^{i}tre--Tolman--Bondi (LTB) spacetimes is provided in terms of various curvature-related geometric properties and physical characteristics. Finally, a noteworthy conclusion of the entire study is presented.
tldr: This paper studies curvature properties, pseudosymmetries, and Ricci solitons of FLRW spacetime, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To fill a gap in differential geometry literature regarding curvature conditions of FLRW spacetime.
method: Mathematical analysis using tensor calculus and curvature conditions.
result: FLRW spacetime satisfies various pseudosymmetric-type conditions and admits almost Ricci soliton and Ricci-Yamabe soliton structures.
conclusion: The study provides a comprehensive geometric characterization of FLRW spacetime and compares it with LTB spacetime.

title: Entropy-Compatible Barrier Schemes For Diffusive Fene Flows
authors: Sai Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: FENE-type conformation-tensor models impose a finite-extensibility constraint that is absent from Oldroyd--B flow: the conformation tensor must satisfy [MATH] and [MATH]. Positive definiteness alone is therefore insufficient, since a numerical state can remain positive while crossing the singular trace barrier. Even a trace-preserving logarithmic parametrization is not enough by itself: high-order reconstruction can remain inside the finite-extensibility domain while injecting artificial FENE entropy. We develop and analyze a barrier-preserving entropy-compatible discretization for FENE-P type flows with polymer center-of-mass molecular diffusion and for trace-singular FENE-family closures with the same entropy structure. The method combines a trace-barrier free energy, a finite-extensibility logarithmic parametrization, a least-damping entropy-compatible barrier-log reconstruction, molecular diffusion paired with the barrier entropy variable, compatible quadrature for polymeric work, and a scaled FENE stress variable for the small-Weissenberg limit. For admissible discrete states we prove finite-extensibility preservation at entropy quadrature points, existence and bisection computability of the maximal entropy-admissible reconstruction parameter, a fully discrete free-energy inequality with relaxation and molecular-diffusion barrier dissipation, a quantitative AP stress closure, and a fixed-discretization Newtonian limit. A conditional relative-entropy estimate is derived on compact subsets of the finite-extensibility domain. Numerical diagnostics verify barrier preservation, entropy-compatible reconstruction, energy decay, AP closure, coupled velocity--pressure--stress accuracy, and high-Weissenberg robustness near the trace constraint.
tldr: This paper develops entropy-compatible numerical schemes for FENE-type polymer flow models, focusing on preserving finite-extensibility constraints and thermodynamic consistency.
motivation: Standard numerical methods for FENE-type flows can violate the finite-extensibility constraint or introduce artificial entropy, motivating the need for barrier-preserving, entropy-compatible discretizations.
method: The method combines a trace-barrier free energy, logarithmic parametrization, entropy-compatible reconstruction, molecular diffusion paired with barrier entropy variables, compatible quadrature, and a scaled stress variable for small Weissenberg numbers.
result: The scheme provably preserves finite-extensibility at quadrature points, satisfies a discrete free-energy inequality, achieves asymptotic-preserving stress closure, and demonstrates robustness near the trace constraint in numerical tests.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for simulating FENE-type flows with guaranteed physical constraints and entropy stability, with potential extensions to more complex viscoelastic models.

title: Umbral Methods, Function Factorisation And Generalisation Of The Fourier Transform Method
authors: Giuseppe Dattoli, Roberto Ricci, Tommaso Severati
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a systematic way to construct trigonometric-like functions beyond the classical sine--cosine pair by factorising rational umbral operators. The guiding idea is simple: the usual trigonometric functions may be viewed as cyclic components arising from a finite factorisation, and the same principle can be extended to an [MATH]-fold decomposition of rational umbral expressions. For each integer [MATH], the construction produces [MATH] functions which play the role of higher-order trigonometric components: their sum reconstructs the corresponding umbral function, while the individual components isolate the different cyclic sectors of its expansion. The construction is developed first in the formal umbral setting. The quadratic case [MATH] gives the Gaussian trigonometric functions, in which the cosine-like component is a Gaussian and the sine-like component is its natural umbral companion. The cubic case [MATH] yields a three-component cyclic system and shows how the same idea extends beyond the usual even--odd decomposition. These examples suggest that trigonometric factorisation is not restricted to ordinary rotations, but belongs to a broader cyclic principle in umbral calculus. We then reinterpret the same formal identities through the recently developed analytic umbral framework. In this second step, the cyclic components are realised by Mellin--Barnes pairings, and the root-of-unity decomposition is related to the splitting of the corresponding spectral kernel. This analytic formulation provides contour representations, local expansions, and sectorial asymptotics for the functions obtained formally. Finally, we indicate how the same cyclic kernels act on Fourier transforms. The resulting framework presents higher-order umbral trigonometric functions as natural cyclic components of factorised rational or exponential umbral operators.
tldr: This paper develops a formal umbral calculus framework to construct generalized trigonometric functions via factorisation of rational umbral operators, with analytic realisations using Mellin-Barnes integrals.
motivation: To extend the concept of trigonometric functions beyond the classical sine-cosine pair by exploiting factorisation of umbral operators, aiming to uncover a broader cyclic principle in umbral calculus.
method: The authors first construct higher-order trigonometric functions in a formal umbral setting by factorising rational umbral operators into cyclic components. They then reinterpret these identities using analytic umbral calculus, employing Mellin-Barnes pairings and root-of-unity decompositions to obtain contour representations and asymptotics.
result: They produce families of functions for any integer n that act as higher-order trigonometric components, with the quadratic case yielding Gaussian trigonometric functions and the cubic case a three-component cyclic system. The analytic formulation provides sectorial asymptotics and spectral kernel splitting.
conclusion: The work suggests that trigonometric factorisation is a general cyclic principle in umbral calculus, with potential applications to Fourier transforms and special functions, but no direct connections to the user's research interests are evident.

title: Analytic Umbral Transmutations And Bessel Moments
authors: Giuseppe Dattoli Roberto Ricci
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an analytic umbral approach to Bessel moments, using them as a concrete testbed justifying the passage from formal indicial umbral calculus to Mellin--Barnes umbral transmutation theory. [...] While the formal procedure reproduces the correct results in suitable convergence chambers, it may lead to non-admissible hypergeometric expansions at physically relevant parameter values. The cubic moment provides the basic example [...] We show that this obstruction is removed by replacing the purely formal expansion with an analytic umbral transmutation. In this setting, exponential umbral pairings are interpreted through Mellin--Barnes integrals, and Ramanujan's Master Theorem acts as an inverse selection principle for the spectral ground state, or clock, associated with a given Bessel product. The factorisation \(J_0^3=J_0J_0^2\) produces two distinct clocks and reduces the cubic full-line moment to a one-dimensional Barnes integral, equivalently to a Meijer \(G\)-function. This gives the classical value of the cubic Bessel moment and clarifies why the divergent Appell realisation is only a local representation of a globally meaningful umbral identity. The same mechanism is then applied to scaled cubic products and to the fourth Bessel moment. [...] The fifth moment marks the first genuinely higher-rank case: the natural umbral grouping leads to a bivariate Barnes transmutation rather than to an ordinary Meijer \(G\)-function. Finally, we discuss real fractional powers \(J_0^\alpha\), \(\alpha>2\), showing that the same interpretation persists beyond integer moments. [...] The resulting picture identifies Bessel moments as values of effective umbral transmutations and separates the global analytic meaning of the umbral representation from the local convergence properties of its hypergeometric residue expansions.
tldr: The paper develops an analytic umbral approach to compute Bessel moments, focusing on mathematical techniques rather than physical applications.
motivation: To resolve issues with formal umbral expansions that yield non-admissible hypergeometric series for Bessel moments, and to provide a rigorous analytic framework.
method: Uses Mellin-Barnes integrals, Ramanujan's Master Theorem, and umbral transmutation to derive closed-form expressions for Bessel moments.
result: Shows that cubic and higher Bessel moments can be expressed as Meijer G-functions or bivariate Barnes integrals, avoiding divergent series.
conclusion: The analytic umbral approach provides a globally valid representation of Bessel moments, with implications for special function theory but limited direct connection to quantum physics.

title: Bounded Deep Unfolding For Joint Beamforming And Scheduling In Multi-Cell Mimo Networks
authors: Jiansheng Li, Shuqi Chai, Fan Xu, Kaiming Shen, Guangxu Zhu, Junting Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the joint resource block group (RBG) scheduling and beamforming optimization problem for weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization in multi-cell multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) downlink networks. While the Fast Fractional Programming (FastFP) framework provides a reliable model-driven solution, it suffers from conservative continuous beamforming updates and prohibitive computational overhead during the discrete RBG matching phase. To address these bottlenecks, we propose a joint deep unfolding framework comprising two core modules: P-Net and K-Net. For continuous beamforming, P-Net learns an adaptive relaxation factor along the analytical FastFP update direction. By strictly constraining this factor within an ascent-preserving interval, P-Net accelerates the optimization trajectory while rigorously retaining monotonic improvement and stationary-point convergence guarantees. For discrete RBG scheduling, K-Net learns a long-horizon priority policy that guides a low-complexity greedy assignment, effectively preserving the assignment quality while bypassing the high complexity of Hungarian matching. Both networks leverage analytical algorithmic priors and utilize recurrent parameter sharing, enabling flexible inference beyond the training horizon. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed joint framework achieves higher WSR and faster execution times than conventional model-driven baselines, while generalizing robustly across unseen network scales, antenna configurations, and channel conditions without retraining.
tldr: This paper proposes a deep unfolding framework for joint beamforming and scheduling in multi-cell MIMO networks to maximize weighted sum-rate.
motivation: Existing model-driven solutions like FastFP suffer from conservative updates and high computational overhead in discrete scheduling.
method: Two neural modules (P-Net and K-Net) are designed: P-Net learns an adaptive relaxation factor for beamforming updates with convergence guarantees, while K-Net learns a priority policy for greedy scheduling.
result: The proposed framework achieves higher weighted sum-rate and faster execution than baselines, and generalizes to unseen network scales and configurations without retraining.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the effectiveness of deep unfolding for resource allocation in wireless networks, but is not directly related to the user's research interests.

title: X-Band UAV-enabled Integrated Sensing And Communications For Vehicular Networks
authors: Soumaya Cherkaoui Remon Polus
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly considered as aerial platforms capable of providing both sensing and communication services, representing a promising paradigm for intelligent transportation systems. This paper investigates the optimal time allocation for a UAV-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISaC) system operating in the X-band for vehicular networks. We analyze the trade-off between sensing accuracy and communication performance under practical UAV constraints and fading effects, considering both single-shadowing and double-shadowing channel models. An optimization framework is developed to allocate time between sensing and communication while guaranteeing minimum communication rates and sufficient sensing reliability. Simulation results demonstrate adaptive time allocation strategies, highlighting how UAV-to-ground channel conditions and target distances influence the balance between sensing and communication in smart mobility scenarios.
tldr: This paper studies time allocation for UAV-based integrated sensing and communication in vehicular networks, focusing on X-band performance trade-offs.
motivation: To optimize the balance between sensing accuracy and communication throughput in UAV-enabled intelligent transportation systems.
method: An optimization framework is developed to allocate time between sensing and communication under practical UAV constraints and fading effects, considering single- and double-shadowing channel models.
result: Adaptive time allocation strategies are demonstrated, showing how channel conditions and target distances influence the sensing-communication trade-off.
conclusion: The work provides insights for designing UAV-based ISaC systems in smart mobility, but does not address quantum or thermodynamic aspects.

title: Learning Implicit Feasibility Constraints For Real-World Routing And Scheduling: Application To Log Transportation
authors: Abdelhakim Abdellaoui, Ayoub Boufous, Issmail El Hallaoui, Loubna Benabbou, Francois Aub\'e, Mouloud Amazouz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world vehicle routing and scheduling problems involve complex operational rules and feasibility constraints typically formulated as mixed-integer linear programs (MILP). However, optimization tools are built around a fixed set of hard-coded constraints, while in practice this set evolves as new rules or preferences emerge, seasonally or permanently. Updating it requires modeling and operations research skills that planners rarely have, so generated plans are routinely adjusted by hand based on practical knowledge. Building on recent work that uses machine learning to recover such hidden constraints, we propose a data-driven constraint-learning approach that trains three complementary predictors, a Graph Neural Network (GNN), a decision tree, and a linear regression, on historical execution data from a log-truck routing and scheduling problem ([MATH]), and embeds each inside a MILP through linearized constraints. We further introduce a stacking mechanism that combines all three within a single augmented optimization problem (AOP), letting the solver endogenously select the most reliable predictor for each decision. On real-world industrial data, each predictor already improves feasibility, but the stacked embedding consistently achieves the lowest objective degradation: it (i)~satisfies the operational rules on unseen instances with smaller degradation than any single-model variant, (ii)~picks the most appropriate predictor per decision without prior knowledge of the rule's nature, and (iii)~reduces daily manual adjustment effort while remaining tractable for daily use. Beyond this application, the framework enables optimization tools that adapt to evolving practice without recurrent manual remodeling.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to learn implicit feasibility constraints for log-truck routing and scheduling, embedding predictors into a MILP to reduce manual adjustments.
motivation: Real-world routing problems have evolving operational rules that are hard to update in optimization tools, leading to manual plan adjustments.
method: Trains a GNN, decision tree, and linear regression on historical data, then embeds each as linearized constraints in a MILP, with a stacking mechanism to select the best predictor per decision.
result: The stacked embedding achieves the lowest objective degradation while satisfying operational rules on unseen instances, reducing manual adjustment effort.
conclusion: The framework enables optimization tools to adapt to evolving rules without manual remodeling, with potential applications beyond log transportation.

title: Bayesian Equilibria Of Heterogeneous Non-Atomic Routing Games With Private Information
authors: Alexia Ambrogio, Leonardo Cianfanelli, Giacomo Como, Paolo Frasca
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study non-atomic Bayesian routing games whereby a transportation network is shared by two types of traffic: a coordinated fleet and a mass of selfish users. The links in the network are characterized by travel time functions that depend both on the aggregate flow on the link and on a random state of the world [MATH] that, in general, is not directly observable. Rather, we assume that both the fleet coordinator and the selfish users know the prior distribution of [MATH], observe (different) private messages that are correlated with [MATH] and possibly among themselves, and make routing decisions based on such heterogeneous partial information. Under the assumption that both the state of the world and the private message sets are finite, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a Bayesian equilibrium for the ensuing Bayesian routing game.
tldr: This paper studies Bayesian equilibria in non-atomic routing games with heterogeneous private information, focusing on transportation networks with coordinated and selfish users.
motivation: To understand how partial and heterogeneous information affects routing decisions and equilibrium existence in transportation networks.
method: The authors model the problem as a Bayesian routing game with finite state and message spaces, and prove existence and uniqueness of Bayesian equilibrium using fixed-point arguments.
result: Existence and uniqueness of a Bayesian equilibrium are established under the assumption of finite state and message sets.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for analyzing routing games with private information, but its direct application to quantum information or thermodynamics is not evident.

title: The Complex Spectral Flow: Spectral Conditions For Two-Parameter Equivariant Bifurcation Guarantees
authors: Ziad Ghanem
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the -- a virtual [MATH]-representation assembling the eigenvalue winding numbers of the linearization at an isolated two-parameter critical point for [MATH] bifurcation problems -- and prove that, for maximal twisted orbit types, the coefficient of the local bifurcation invariant in [MATH] reduces to a closed-form dimension formula, bypassing the standard pipeline of basic degree factorization and Burnside ring multiplication entirely. When the eigenvalue dependence is holomorphic, topological cancellation among winding numbers is impossible, yielding unconditional local and global bifurcation guarantees. As applications, we establish the macroscopic escape of symmetric Hopf branches in [MATH]-equivariant systems and of patterned relative equilibria for the complex Ginzburg--Landau equation directly from spectral data.
tldr: This paper introduces a virtual representation for eigenvalue winding numbers in two-parameter equivariant bifurcation problems, providing a closed-form dimension formula for bifurcation invariants.
motivation: To simplify the computation of local bifurcation invariants in two-parameter equivariant systems, bypassing the standard pipeline of basic degree factorization and Burnside ring multiplication.
method: The authors define a virtual representation that assembles eigenvalue winding numbers and prove that for maximal twisted orbit types, the coefficient of the local bifurcation invariant reduces to a closed-form dimension formula.
result: Topological cancellation among winding numbers is impossible when eigenvalue dependence is holomorphic, yielding unconditional bifurcation guarantees. Applications include symmetric Hopf branches and patterned relative equilibria for the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation.
conclusion: The work provides a spectral approach to bifurcation analysis that simplifies computations and offers unconditional guarantees for holomorphic dependencies, with potential applications in equivariant dynamical systems.

title: Sequence Reconstruction For Substitution Channel: New Sufficient Conditions And Algorithms
authors: Chen Wang, Eitan Yaakobi, Yiwei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the sequence reconstruction problem, a codeword [MATH] is transmitted through several identical channels where each channel produces a noisy read of [MATH], and the problem is to analyze how to uniquely reconstruct [MATH] based on these noisy reads. Levenshtein has studied the minimum number of reads which guarantees unique reconstruction of [MATH], which is one sufficient condition for unique reconstruction. In this paper, we move on to a different perspective and propose a new framework for unique reconstruction. Our new sufficient condition for unique reconstruction takes both the number of reads and the distances among the reads into consideration. We offer both theoretical analysis and corresponding efficient reconstruction algorithms for our reconstruction framework.
tldr: This paper studies sequence reconstruction from noisy reads over substitution channels, proposing new sufficient conditions and algorithms for unique reconstruction.
motivation: To improve upon Levenshtein's sufficient condition for unique reconstruction by considering both the number of reads and their distances.
method: The authors propose a new framework that incorporates distances among reads, and develop efficient reconstruction algorithms based on this framework.
result: New sufficient conditions for unique reconstruction are derived, and corresponding algorithms are provided with theoretical analysis.
conclusion: The work offers a more flexible approach to sequence reconstruction, with potential applications in DNA storage and communication.

title: A Two-Channel F-Transform Representation For Early Trajectory Characterization In Iterated Correlation Dynamics
authors: Ishrak Alhajj Hassan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many nonlinear iterative procedures generate high-dimensional trajectories whose early behavior is informative but difficult to compare directly. This paper studies a soft-computing representation problem: how to convert a short early trajectory segment into compact, interpretable, fixed-dimensional fuzzy coordinates that preserve information about subsequent convergence and trajectory geometry. The problem is investigated for iterated Pearson correlation matrices, a nonlinear matrix iteration historically connected with CONCOR-type blockmodeling and repeated-correlation methods. The proposed descriptor uses two logarithmic signals from the early post-transient regime: a step-size signal, measuring contraction magnitude, and a contraction-ratio signal, measuring local contraction evolution. Each signal is projected onto a three-node triangular fuzzy partition using zero-degree F-transform coefficients and one centered first-degree coefficient. This yields an eight-dimensional two-channel representation separating local level from local trend and contraction magnitude from contraction evolution. Across 22 matrix dimensions with 1000 trajectories per dimension, the descriptor is compared with raw trajectory samples, statistical summaries, and PCA-compressed raw features using Random Forest regression for convergence-length approximation. It achieves mean R^2 = 0.6480, close to raw trajectories (0.6518) and statistical summaries (0.6528), while improving over the step-size-only F-transform descriptor (0.5001). Repeated random-split and shifted-window experiments confirm stability. PCA and clustering further show reproducible low-dimensional organization, with the first two principal components explaining 84.26% of variance and k = 3 favored by the mean silhouette criterion.
tldr: This paper proposes a fuzzy-transform-based descriptor for early trajectory characterization in iterated correlation dynamics, achieving compact representation with competitive convergence prediction accuracy.
motivation: To convert short early trajectory segments from nonlinear iterative procedures into compact, interpretable fuzzy coordinates that preserve information about subsequent convergence and trajectory geometry.
method: Two logarithmic signals (step-size and contraction-ratio) from the early post-transient regime are projected onto triangular fuzzy partitions using zero-degree and first-degree F-transform coefficients, forming an eight-dimensional two-channel representation. Random Forest regression is used for convergence-length approximation.
result: The descriptor achieves mean R^2 = 0.6480, close to raw trajectories (0.6518) and statistical summaries (0.6528), and improves over step-size-only F-transform (0.5001). PCA shows 84.26% variance explained by first two components, and clustering favors k=3.
conclusion: The proposed representation is effective for early trajectory characterization in iterated correlation dynamics, with potential applications in soft computing and data analysis, but no direct connection to the user's research interests.

title: Optimal Experimental Design For Passive Imaging Source Problems
authors: Christian Aarset, Thorsten Hohage, Georg Stadler
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work focuses on optimal experimental design (OED) methods for passive imaging. We adopt a Bayesian inverse problem framework for passive imaging source problems, primarily focusing on spatially uncorrelated sources and systems governed by the Helmholtz equation. A major challenge in passive imaging is that the use of correlation data causes the observation dimension to grow quadratically with the number of sensor locations, compounding the computational difficulty of finding optimal designs. To overcome the computational bottleneck of repeated PDE solves in optimal design algorithms, we develop a two-level, low-rank approximation of the A-optimal design objective. This effectively decouples the problem into an offline and an online phase, enabling efficient evaluation of the design objective and its gradient without additional PDE solves. Our numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm efficiently scales to large problems and that the resulting optimal designs significantly outperform random sensor placements in minimizing posterior uncertainty.
tldr: This paper develops optimal experimental design methods for passive imaging source problems using Bayesian inverse problems and low-rank approximations, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Passive imaging source problems suffer from high computational cost due to quadratic growth of correlation data with sensor count; efficient design algorithms are needed.
method: A two-level, low-rank approximation of the A-optimal design objective is developed, decoupling the problem into offline and online phases to avoid repeated PDE solves.
result: The algorithm scales efficiently to large problems and optimal designs significantly outperform random sensor placements in minimizing posterior uncertainty.
conclusion: The proposed method enables practical OED for passive imaging, but the work is entirely classical and unrelated to quantum systems or information thermodynamics.

title: Robust Repair Of Reed-Solomon Codes
authors: Wilton Kim, Stanislav Kruglik, Gaojun Luo, Han Mao Kiah
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of robust repair of a single erasure in Reed--Solomon codes under low communication bandwidth. Focusing on the Guruswami--Wootters trace repair framework, we investigate whether a failed node can be correctly repaired in the presence of erroneous responses from helper nodes. Equivalently, we view the collection of downloaded traces as a code, which we call the repair-trace code. By characterizing the zero coefficients of the associated polynomial in terms of cyclotomic cosets, we derive upper bounds on the dimension [MATH] that allow correction of a given number of erroneous traces [MATH], as well as lower bounds on the minimum distance as a function of [MATH]. For the case [MATH], we exploit explicit formulas for cyclotomic coset representatives to obtain the exact optimal dimension bound for single-error correction. We also propose two efficient robust repair schemes. Our first scheme achieves the error-correction capability guaranteed by the BCH bound. To approach a stronger bound based on character sums, we develop a second scheme that tolerates more errors at the cost of an additional factor [MATH] in computational complexity.
tldr: This paper studies robust repair of Reed-Solomon codes under erroneous helper responses, focusing on the Guruswami-Wootters trace repair framework.
motivation: To ensure correct repair of a failed node in distributed storage systems even when some helper nodes provide erroneous responses.
method: Characterizes zero coefficients of associated polynomials via cyclotomic cosets to derive bounds on repair-trace code dimension and minimum distance; proposes two efficient robust repair schemes.
result: Derives upper and lower bounds on dimension for error correction, obtains exact optimal dimension for single-error correction, and proposes schemes achieving BCH bound and a stronger character-sum bound.
conclusion: Provides theoretical bounds and practical schemes for robust repair of Reed-Solomon codes, with trade-offs between error tolerance and computational complexity.

title: Multi-parameter Persistence In Dynamical Systems For Maximizing Effects Of Control Inputs
authors: Tomoo Yokoyama Yusuke Imoto
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new topological method to naturally extend a partial function [MATH] on a ``generalization'' of a metric space [MATH] equipped with a dynamical system [MATH], to a function [MATH] with parameters [MATH], which allows us to apply existing topological data analysis techniques to functions defined on the whole space. Moreover, given a function [MATH] that evaluates the ``quality'' of points within [MATH], using this extended function, one can construct a sufficient condition for the existence of an optimal [MATH]-perturbation path from any point into [MATH] that minimizes the value of [MATH] under the condition [MATH]. In addition, if the domain [MATH] is finite, then the function [MATH] can be computed recursively. As an application, for a given partial evaluation function on a space equipped with a dynamical system, one can construct a three-parameter filtration associated with its extension, which naturally identifies minimal paths. This clarifies the relationship among three factors: the evaluation of the cost norm, the strength of control, and the resulting value.
tldr: This paper introduces a topological method to extend partial functions on dynamical systems for optimizing control inputs, with applications to path planning.
motivation: To develop a framework that uses topological data analysis to find optimal perturbation paths in dynamical systems under cost constraints.
method: The authors extend partial functions on metric spaces with dynamical systems to full functions with parameters, enabling the application of persistent homology. They construct a three-parameter filtration to identify minimal paths.
result: A sufficient condition for the existence of optimal perturbation paths is derived, and a recursive computation is possible for finite domains.
conclusion: The method clarifies the trade-off between cost norm, control strength, and resulting value, offering a new tool for control optimization in dynamical systems.

title: Energy Efficiency Optimization For Rotatable Antenna-Enabled Uplink Noma Systems
authors: Yixuan Li, Jun Wang, Hongbo Xu, Ji Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates a rotatable antenna (RA)-enabled uplink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system, where a base station equipped with multiple independently RAs serves both ground and aerial users. Specifically, we formulate an energy efficiency (EE) maximization problem by jointly optimizing receive beamforming, user power allocation, and RA rotation. To make the problem tractable, a new block coordinate descent-based algorithm is developed, in which the receive beamforming is updated via the minimum mean square error criterion, while the power allocation and RA rotation are handled by fractional programming and successive convex approximation. Numerical results demonstrate the EE superiority of the proposed RA-NOMA scheme over several benchmarks.
tldr: This paper optimizes energy efficiency in a rotatable antenna-enabled uplink NOMA system using joint beamforming, power allocation, and antenna rotation.
motivation: To improve energy efficiency in wireless communication systems with rotatable antennas and NOMA, addressing the need for higher spectral and energy efficiency in future networks.
method: A block coordinate descent algorithm is developed, updating receive beamforming via MMSE, and handling power allocation and RA rotation via fractional programming and successive convex approximation.
result: The proposed RA-NOMA scheme achieves superior energy efficiency compared to several benchmarks.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the potential of combining rotatable antennas with NOMA for energy-efficient uplink communications, with implications for future wireless system design.

title: Asymmetry Of Entropy Invariants For Generic Mixing $Z^n$-Actions
authors: Valery V. Ryzhikov Mikhail V. Engelgardt
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose that for a mixing [MATH]-action, [MATH], there exists a Kirillov-Kushnirenko entropy that is zero for this action and completely positive for its inverse. We prove that this property is generic for the mixing [MATH]-actions.
tldr: The paper proves that for generic mixing Z^n-actions, the Kirillov-Kushnirenko entropy can be zero for the action and completely positive for its inverse, demonstrating asymmetry of entropy invariants.
motivation: To understand the asymmetry of entropy invariants under inversion for mixing Z^n-actions, which is a fundamental question in ergodic theory.
method: The authors use generic properties of mixing actions and entropy theory, likely employing Baire category arguments and constructions of mixing actions with prescribed entropy behavior.
